Sure, I can do that, fren!: Manus 2.0 adds a rebuilt agent engine, a desktop creation workspace, editable video and game-development tools, event-triggered automations, remote computer control, and a separate personal-agent app called Cue. It launched on September 28, 2026, and is available on web, desktop, and mobile.[1]

## Main features

| Feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| Cascade | New agent architecture that loads specialized capabilities only when needed, keeping the brief, website, video, and automation connected within one project. [1] |
| Manus Studio | Upgraded desktop workspace for documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, slides, websites, code, videos, and games. With authorization, it can work directly with your existing local files, folders, and tools. [2][1] |
| Video Editor | Generates a first cut and exposes an editable timeline with separate clips, images, text, motion graphics, and audio. You can change individual elements without regenerating the entire video. [1] |
| Alchemy mode | Video Editor mode that combines video and code generation, with Manus taking on creative direction. The resulting video remains editable on the timeline. [1] |
| Game Dev | Builds games from playable templates using image, video, and coding models. Includes asset management, code editing, live previews, targeted changes, and publishing as a playable website. [2][1] |
| Cloud Computer | A separately purchased, dedicated cloud environment for persistent projects, including multiplayer game servers and always-running automations. [1] |
| Automations | Starts workflows when events occur in connected services—not just at scheduled times. Examples include email, calendar events, Slack messages, Notion updates, and changes in advertising performance. [1] |
| Remote Control | Lets you give instructions by voice from your phone while watching a live view of your desktop as Manus performs the task. [2] |
| Computer Use | Powers authorized interaction with approved files, browsers, and applications in a visible, separate workspace on your computer. [2] |
| Cue | Separate personal-agent app: each agent has its own email, phone number, wallet, and computer. Multiple agents can collaborate in a shared group chat. [1] |

## What changes in practice

The biggest shift is **editability**: Manus produces a starting point, then lets you make precise changes yourself and hand the same project back to the agent. For example, you can replace generated product footage with your own recording, swap the music, adjust an animation, and ask Manus to refine the remaining video without losing those edits. Video Editor targets short product ads, AI-generated user-style content, tutorials, vlogs, and motion graphics; product ads are typically 30–60 seconds.[2][1]

Game Dev follows the same approach. You can change one character’s appearance, movement, or scene without resetting the rest of the project. Multiplayer support connects to a purchased Cloud Computer, with Manus handling the hosting and networking setup.[1]

Automations also move beyond “run this every morning.” A connected-service event can start work immediately. The help center’s example watches a product account on X and prepares a summary and sample prompts when an update appears, leaving the user to decide what gets published.[2]

## Performance claims

Manus reports that Cascade achieved the following against its previous system in **one** tested configuration:

- 23.2% fewer tokens.
- 28.2% less time to finish tasks.
- 32% lower running cost.[2]

Those figures are not an overall average, guaranteed speedup, or promise that subscription prices have dropped by 32%. The official documentation specifically limits them to that tested configuration.[2]

## Availability and limits

Cloud Computer is an additional purchase, rather than a free server included with every project. Local computer access requires a connected, authorized session and approved resources.[2]

Cue is a separate early-access product requiring an invitation code. Its agents can make payments within a user-set budget and pass work between teammates. The launch announcement said its iOS release was pending App Store review; it does not establish that review has since finished.[1]
